name: Killdozer
label: Touch and Go
lede: Three guys from Madison named themselves after a TV movie about a killer bulldozer, dedicated an EP to a folk singer who wasn't dead, made Butch Vig's name before Nirvana did, and quit on a tour called Fuck You, We Quit!

eras.title: Basements, beer and cigars
eras.text: Three guys in Madison, Wisconsin wrote slow, crushing songs about the people around them: bikers without bikes, hoarders, drunks, Ed Gein. They cut them at a little studio run by Butch Vig and Steve Marker, years before either was famous.

q: I cultivated my voice with beer and cigars.
years.h: Killdozer forms in Madison, named for a killer bulldozer movie
years.p: Singer and bassist [[Michael Gerald|bedbb6eb-bd46-4643-819f-8db9ef6564c9]], guitarist Bill Hobson and his brother, drummer Dan Hobson, name themselves after Killdozer!, a 1974 TV movie about a possessed bulldozer. Their first basement shows in Madison came before they had the name.
years.xp: Gerald's growl started as a rehearsal joke; the Hobson brothers insisted he use it on everything, and Butch Vig talked him out of trying to sing straight. The songs, Gerald said, were meant to make his friends laugh.

years.src: Wikipedia: Intellectuals Are the Shoeshine Boys of the Ruling Elite
years.h: Intellectuals Are the Shoeshine Boys of the Ruling Elite
years.p: Killdozer's debut, recorded in November 1983 at Smart Studio in Madison with Steve Marker and Butch Vig, comes out on Bone Air Records. Touch and Go reissued it in 1989.
years.xp: The only cover is Creedence Clearwater Revival's Run Through the Jungle. Maximumrocknroll heard jazzy-metal playing, extremely gruff vocals and smart-ass lyrics.
play: Intellectuals Are the Shoeshine Boys of the Ruling Elite

years.h: Snakeboy, Killdozer's first album for Touch and Go
years.p: Recorded in March 1985 at Smart Studio in Madison with Steve Marker, Butch Vig and Duke Erikson. Much of Snakeboy is about Michael Gerald's encounter with a man named Bill Reisman.
years.xp: The only cover is Neil Young's Cinnamon Girl, and Jessica Noll plays violin on River. Vig remixed King of Sex for a 2006 tribute album.

eras.title: Burl Ives wasn't dead yet
eras.text: Killdozer kept its day jobs and made a record a year, including a memorial EP for a man who was still alive and a covers album that crawled through American Pie. One of them got Butch Vig the call that changed his life.

years.h: Burl, dedicated to Burl Ives, who was still alive
years.p: Killdozer dedicates the Burl EP to the memory of folk singer Burl Ives, who hadn't died. He died in 1995. The Wisconsin Boys Choir sings backup on the Jessi Colter cover I'm Not Lisa.
years.xp: It was recorded at Multi-Trac in Detroit, with Touch and Go's [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] and Butch Vig producing. Vig told Isthmus that people kept trying to break into the place, and Rusk stood outside with a cattle prod.

years.src: Wikipedia: Little Baby Buntin' · The Vinyl District
years.h: Little Baby Buntin' and the biker gang with no bikes
years.p: Killdozer's third album includes The Puppy, which Michael Gerald based on a Madison gang called Satan's Dragons whose members didn't own motorcycles. There's also a Neil Diamond cover.
years.xp: Gerald said the song grew out of a real initiation that went horribly wrong. The Vinyl District's obituary of the band calls Killdozer the greatest protest band ever.

years.h: For Ladies Only: nine covers, and an 8:45 American Pie
years.p: Killdozer's all-covers album, cut at Smart Studio with Butch Vig, drags Don McLean's American Pie, Arthur Alexander's Burnin' Love and the Steve Miller Band's Take the Money and Run through the sludge.
years.xp: Besides LP, CD and a picture disc, it came as a box of five colored 7" singles with a bonus cover of Neil Young's Mr. Soul. NME gave it 9 out of 10.

years.h: Twelve Point Buck gets Butch Vig the Nirvana job
years.p: Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman heard Killdozer's Twelve Point Buck and sent [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] to Butch Vig to record demos. Kurt Cobain later wanted Nevermind to sound as heavy as this album.
years.xp:
Vig told Isthmus the record opened a lot of doors, and that Poneman wanted that attitude for Nirvana. It reached No. 16 on the UK indie chart; the Washington Post called its thump-and-grind art music.

Wikipedia says the album also brought Vig to [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]]'s attention before [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]]' Gish.

years.h: Bill Hobson quits Killdozer, twice, and the band stops
years.p: Bill Hobson leaves before a European tour and AmRep boss Tom Hazelmyer of Halo of Flies fills in. Hobson returns, then walks out during a recording session, AllMusic says, and Killdozer goes quiet.
years.xp: Michael Gerald's tour diary from the period ran in Your Flesh in winter 1990, with notes on cold Iowa, Old Style half-barrels and the joy of a day that starts at Waffle House.

eras.title: Trotskyites with a bulldozer
eras.text: Michael Gerald and Dan Hobson came back with a new guitarist and a new target. The album titles turned into Marxist slogans, Steve Albini recorded the last one, and by the end Gerald was the only founder left.

years.h: Killdozer returns with guitarist Paul Zagoras
years.p: Michael Gerald and Dan Hobson restart Killdozer with Paul Zagoras on guitar and release the single The Pig Was Cool.

years.h: Uncompromising War on Art: a comeback titled like a pamphlet
years.p: Killdozer's return album is Uncompromising War on Art Under the Dictatorship of the Proletariat. Michael Gerald called himself a Trotskyite, The Vinyl District reported.
years.xp: The CD adds the whole Burl EP, with liner notes admitting Burl Ives hadn't died yet and might still be alive.

years.src: Wikipedia: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent
years.h: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent, recorded by Steve Albini
years.p: Killdozer's last studio album is cut in September 1994 at the House That Dripped Blood in Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The only cover is Lee Hazlewood's Pour Man.
years.xp: The Washington Post heard an alternate universe where Black Sabbath taught Robert Johnson the blues. The Chicago Tribune called it uproariously brutish, heavy and slow.
play: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent

years.h: Dan Hobson leaves; Erik Tunison and Jeff Ditzenberger join
years.p: Drummer Dan Hobson leaves Killdozer to focus on his family, AllMusic says. Erik Tunison of [[Die Kreuzen|7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e]] takes the drums and Jeff Ditzenberger of Power Wagon joins on second guitar.

years.src: Rebel Noise · Chicago Reader · Wikipedia: Killdozer
years.h: Killdozer's farewell tour is called Fuck You, We Quit!
years.p: Michael Gerald, the last founder standing, ends Killdozer with a tour officially titled Fuck You, We Quit! He said he wanted to pursue other interests.
years.xp: Gerald recalled that some longtime fans at the last shows needed babysitters to get there. The same year Killdozer shared a split, Michael Gerald's Party Machine Presents!, with Alice Donut, a band Gerald had met at a Berlin disco.

eras.title: Fuck You, We Reunite!
eras.text: After the farewell the founders scattered into tax law, film crews and nursing. Touch and Go's 25th birthday brought the original trio back, under a rule that the band could never get in the way of the day jobs.

years.h: The Last Waltz, a live Killdozer farewell on Man's Ruin
years.p: Man's Ruin Records releases a live album from Killdozer's last run. Crustacean Records reissues it in 2006.

years.h: Michael Gerald becomes a tax lawyer, helped by Big Black
years.p: Michael Gerald got into NYU Law with a three-page essay about his Killdozer career and a recommendation from [[Santiago Durango|00aa2c29-22a9-4e55-a01b-e51896a379a3]], ex-[[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] guitarist turned lawyer. In 2003 he was a tax lawyer in Los Angeles.

years.h: Original Killdozer reunites for Touch and Go's 25th
years.p: Michael Gerald and Bill and Dan Hobson play Touch and Go's 25th anniversary block party outside the Hideout in Chicago at 3:50 p.m., billed as Fuck You, We Reunite!
years.xp: By then Gerald was a tax lawyer in Los Angeles, Bill Hobson a film grip there, and Dan Hobson a registered nurse still drumming in Madison bands. The same year, the 28-track tribute We Will Bury You came out with a Butch Vig remix of King of Sex.

q: It can't interfere with our day jobs.
years.h: Killdozer plays Madison's Forward Music Festival
years.p: Killdozer headlines the High Noon Saloon at Madison's Forward Music Festival. Touch and Go sold $35 guaranteed-entry tickets because a $25 festival pass wouldn't get you in if the room filled.
years.xp: Gerald told the Chicago Reader the band would only play if it didn't cost anyone a day job, and that only an insult to someone's dog could break them up.

years.h: Killdozer plays WFMU live on Election Day
years.p: The reunited trio plays a full live set on Brian Turner's show on WFMU, on the night of the 2008 presidential election, during a fall US run.
